metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude chases an overdue invoice, is it improvising case by case, or following a fixed written procedure? Lands the carry-out that a Skill is Claude following a written procedure, the same one every run, limited to exactly what that file specifies.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed chasing an invoice means Claude guessing case by case. It doesn't — it follows a written procedure. So: does Claude need the right steps, not the right guesses, to chase an invoice?

beats.narration_text: A Skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is invoice-chase — the SKILL.md inside it holds the whole instruction set, plain language, no hidden code. Claude reads the file, then works through it. The file is the program.

The instructions run as steps, in order. Claude reads each one and carries it out, top to bottom — no branching unless the file says so. One flag: we don't have invoice-chase's literal file here, only the shape every Skill shares — read the steps, execute them in order, then return the result.

Here's the constraint worth knowing: since the file is the whole program, Claude can only do what its steps say. Same input, same output, every run — repeatable. But if a client's situation doesn't match any step in the file, Claude has nothing else to reach for. The limit is exactly what the file specifies, nothing more.
A Skill isn't Claude improvising — it's Claude following a written procedure, the same one, every run. The whole limit is what that file says, nothing more.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I run an invoice-chase process for late-paying clients — write me a SKILL.md that spells out the exact steps, no improvising. Then walk me through what you'll do, before you do it. That clause matters: explaining first shows you the actual procedure, not a guess.
